newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen lower after CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen lower after CPI.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening lower on Thursday after a report on the April Consumer Price Index, analysts said.

The data "were a little bit disappointing. Even though the PPI can remain reassuring, the CPI is really going to present a problem, in my opinion. In my opinion, it is more than enough justification for the Fed to move next week," Michael Metz, Chief Investment Strategist at Oppenheimer & Co said.
The CPI rose 0.1 percent in April. Excluding food and energy, the index was up 0.3 percent. Economists had expected overall CPI to rise 0.1 percent and the core rate to rise 0.2 percent.
